prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
API keys, roles and the audit trail are in. `npm test` passes (29 tests) and `npm run lint` is clean. One thing to act on: `data/db.json` has no keys, so the server will answer 401 to everything until you add some.

**Behaviour**
- Every request needs `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A missing or unknown key gets 401 `unauthorized`; a known key without permission gets 403 `forbidden`. Both come back in the usual error shape.
- `viewer` can only GET. `cook` can also `POST /recipes/:id/cook`, `POST /batches/:id/waste`, `POST /temperatures` and `POST /stocktakes/:id/counts`. `manager` can do everything.
- Every authenticated non-GET request writes an audit entry `{id, at, key, method, path, status}`, including ones that end in 403 or an error status. Requests with no valid key are not audited, since there is no key name to record. `GET /audit` lists the entries newest first and only managers can call it.

**Schema 3**
- Keys and audit entries live in the data, so I bumped the schema to 3, as `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` requires. The 2→3 migration adds empty `apiKeys` and `audit` lists and invents no keys.
- `data/seed.json` has one key per role: `viewer-key`, `cook-key` and `manager-key`.
- `data/db.json` is untouched. It still opens, but it has no keys until you add them.

**Tests**
- The test helper now sends the manager key by default, so the existing tests send a key without edits.
- `tests/cli.test.js` expected schema version 2 in two places; both now expect 3.
- I added `tests/auth.test.js`, which covers 401, 403 and the audit order.

I also updated the Routes section of `README.md`, the auth section of `docs/API.md` (both list `GET /audit`) and `CHANGELOG.md`.
